# HUD grey-out for zero-charge power-up rows

## Goal

When a power-up the player owns has zero available charges, render its HUD row (icon + label + value) greyed-out/inactive instead of hiding it; render normally when charges > 0.

## Acceptance Criteria

- When a power-up the player owns has zero available charges, its HUD row is rendered greyed-out/inactive; when charges > 0 the row renders normally.
- Row visibility: an owned Phase Shift/Teleport with an empty pool stays visible (greyed), not hidden; power-ups the player has never owned stay hidden.
- The icon, label and value share one greyed styling derived from a shared grey variant (`src/powerups/icons.ts`), so icon and text cannot diverge.
- Charged rows and all non-charge rows render unchanged.

## Minimal Implementation

- `src/ui/HUD.ts`: `_isPowerUpRowVisible` / `_powerUpStacks` (owned-but-empty → visible + greyed), `_addRow` grey styling, HUD docs.
- `src/powerups/icons.ts`: shared grey variant for the Phase Shift/Teleport icons used by the HUD.

## Dependencies

- Tests: HUD grey-out for empty recharge pools (test-first).
- Wire recharge tick and finite-pool auto-defence.

## Key Files

- src/ui/HUD.ts
- src/powerups/icons.ts

# Document the recharge model (GDD + code comments)

## Goal

Bring the Game Design Document (teleport / phase-shift sections, power-up levelling section, HUD presentation) and the relevant code comments up to date with the recharge model, so the written design matches the shipped behaviour.

## Acceptance Criteria

- The Game Design Document (teleport / phase-shift sections and the power-up levelling section) and relevant code comments are updated to describe the recharge model; the CHANGELOG is managed by the ship skill's release pipeline and is excluded.
- The teleport and phase-shift sections of the Game Design Document describe recharging charge pools (per-charge timers, cap of 3, level-derived recharge time) and no longer claim unlimited activations for the permanent Phase Shift reward.
- The GDD power-up levelling section (§4.4) and HUD presentation describe the new recharge-time axes and the greyed-out-row behaviour for zero-charge pools.
- Relevant code comments in `src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts` and `src/powerups/effects.ts` (module headers, consume/collect/resolver docs) match the recharge model.

## Minimal Implementation

- Edit `docs/Game Design Document.md` (teleport/phase-shift sections, power-up levelling + HUD presentation) and the two module header/comment blocks.
- The three out-of-scope follow-ups (recharge countdown bar, recharge-complete audio cue, gym recharge sliders) are already recorded as sibling work items.

## Dependencies

- HUD grey-out for zero-charge power-up rows (behaviour finalised) and the recharge engine (model finalised).

## Key Files

- docs/Game Design Document.md
- src/powerups/powerUpLevels.ts
- src/powerups/effects.ts

# Steering and forward model consume live thruster values

**Parent:** AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9 · **Issue type:** task · **Priority:** medium

## Goal

The steering candidate prediction (`evaluateDirection` player-speed term) and
the forward-model thrust decision (`mayThrust` friction stopping distance) must
use the snapshot's live values; the tunables `playerSpeed` /
`frictionDeceleration` become **defaults/overrides**, never authoritative.

As a designer editing `frictionDeceleration`/`maxSpeed`, I want the demo bot's
steering and stopping behaviour to track the change without code edits, so I
can validate tuning in a gym or a run.

## Scope

- `evaluateDirection`: use the snapshot's live max speed for the candidate
  speed term, falling back to tunables `playerSpeed`.
- `mayThrust`: use the snapshot's live friction deceleration for stopping
  distance, falling back to tunables `frictionDeceleration`.
- Precedence: explicit `GymBotTuning` override > live `ShipConfig` > compiled
  tunable default.
- Preserve exact default-equivalence: with no config present the decisions are
  bit-for-bit unchanged vs today.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `evaluateDirection`'s candidate-speed term uses the snapshot's live max speed when present, falling back to the `playerSpeed` tunable otherwise.
- `mayThrust` computes stopping distance with the snapshot's live friction deceleration when present, falling back to the `frictionDeceleration` tunable; explicit GymBotTuning overrides still win over live config, which wins over the compiled default (documented precedence).
- With no config in the snapshot the decisions are bit-for-bit identical to today's `playerSpeed: 175` / `frictionDeceleration: 100` constants (default-equivalence preserved).
- At least one unit test pins a pure decision consuming live values and changing the outcome versus the defaults; the fallback-path baseline test stays green.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — `evaluateDirection`, `mayThrust`.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` — `playerSpeed`/`frictionDeceleration` documented as defaults/overrides.
- `src/ai/framework/worldModel.ts` — world view carries the player config (if the term is read from the world).
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.test.ts` — custom-vs-default and fallback tests.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBot.test.ts` — end-to-end decision coverage.

## Dependencies

- Depends on the BotSnapshot thruster-config child (AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9).
- Depends on the test-harness child.

## Out of scope

- Reverse thrust modelling (next child).
- Enemy-bullet fire-prediction tunables.

## References

- Parent intake brief: AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9

# Reverse braking model consumes live reverse thruster values

**Parent:** AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9 · **Issue type:** task · **Priority:** medium

## Goal

Reverse braking must be gated and modelled with the live reverse values:
`asteroidsReverseEnabled` (already respected at snapshot level),
`asteroidsReverseThrustAcceleration` and `asteroidsReverseMaxSpeed` feed the
reverse forward-model instead of being absent.

As a player who re-tuned or disabled my reverse thruster, I want the bot's
reverse braking to use my configured acceleration and speed cap, so the demo
never contradicts the handling I experience.

## Scope

- Feed the live reverse acceleration and/or reverse speed cap into the reverse
  forward-model (brake distance under reverse acceleration and/or reverse
  speed cap).
- Keep the existing `mayReverse` tuning gates (`reverseImminentOvershootGap`,
  `reverseRetreatRange`) as tunables.
- Preserve the trouble/correction semantics from AH-0MV2WJSY70070HK2 (reverse
  is not a general positioning tool).

## Acceptance Criteria

- The reverse forward-model consumes `asteroidsReverseThrustAcceleration` and/or `asteroidsReverseMaxSpeed` from the snapshot to model reverse-assisted braking distance / reverse speed cap, instead of omitting reverse physics entirely.
- Reverse remains gated on the snapshot's live `reverseEnabled`, and the existing `mayReverse` tuning gates (`reverseImminentOvershootGap`, `reverseRetreatRange`) remain tunables.
- The reverse-reserved-for-trouble/correction semantics of AH-0MV2WJSY70070HK2 are preserved (no reverse used for routine positioning).
- Unit tests cover a custom reverse config changing the reverse decision versus defaults, and reverse-disabled behaviour emitting no reverse.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.ts` — `mayReverse` / reverse forward-model.
- `src/ai/botSnapshot.ts` — reverse fields consumed.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` — reverse gate/default docs.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/steering.test.ts` — custom reverse config + disabled tests.

## Dependencies

- Depends on the live thruster-config snapshot child.
- Depends on the test-harness child.
- Related: AH-0MV2WJSY70070HK2 (reverse overuse semantics).

## Out of scope

- A full reverse-kinematics rework beyond the live numeric consumption.

## References

- Parent intake brief: AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9
- AH-0MV2JS18K006YU35 (reverse enable-flag plumbing)

# Tunable demotion, gym parity, docs and full-suite verification

**Parent:** AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9 · **Issue type:** task · **Priority:** medium

## Goal

Complete the refactor: demote the physics tunables to documented defaults,
prove gym↔game parity, update the documentation, and verify the full suite.

As a maintainer, I want the tunables clearly documented as fallback defaults +
overrides, parity enforced between the demo bot and the gym, and the docs to
match the new live-thruster model.

## Scope

- `tunables.ts`: mark `playerSpeed`/`frictionDeceleration` (and any new
  reverse preview defaults) as fallback defaults + tuning overrides, never the
  ship's truth.
- Verify `GymBotTuning` / `toCompetentOverrides` overrides still win over live
  config (same `resolveCompetentTunables` seam as `PlayScene`).
- Update `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` and code comments.
- Run the full project test suite.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `tunables.ts` demotes `playerSpeed`/`frictionDeceleration` (and any new reverse preview defaults) to documented fallback defaults and tuning overrides, never authoritative, with doc comments updated.
- `GymBotTuning` overrides (`toCompetentOverrides`) demonstrably still win over live config for the fields they set, through the same `resolveCompetentTunables` seam as `PlayScene`.
- Gym↔game parity holds: `PlayScene` and the gym scenes exercising the bot share the same snapshot/steering code — no divergent copy (the repo duplicate-body guard and the gym-parity docs assertion pass).
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` and code comments reflect live-thruster consumption and the fallback/override precedence.
- The full project test suite passes with all changes.

## Key Files

- `src/ai/framework/competent/tunables.ts` — default/override docs.
- `src/ai/tuningFields.ts` — tuning-gym field descriptions.
- `src/scenes/gym/GymBotTuning.ts` — parity verification.
- `src/scenes/PlayScene.ts` — parity verification.
- `docs/BOT_FRAMEWORK.md` — documentation.
- `src/ai/framework/competent/competentBotDocs.test.ts` — docs guard.

## Dependencies

- Depends on the steering-consumes-live-values child.
- Depends on the reverse-model child.

## Out of scope

- Deprecating/removing the now-fallback tuning sliders (record as a linked follow-up if desired).

## References

- Parent intake brief: AH-0MV268RXJ007M7A9
- AH-0MUGZDTFX004RBD1 (gym-parity convention)
- AH-0MV4D7LAD009XYR0 (GymBotTuning seam)
